Based on the provided evidence, Michael Jordan’s scoring titles and LeBron James’s all-time scoring record serve as the foundation for two distinct arguments: **peak seasonal scoring dominance** versus **sustained career longevity and consistency**.

---

### 1. Michael Jordan’s Scoring Titles: The Case for Peak Dominance
Jordan’s achievements are used to argue for unprecedented single-season scoring supremacy and peak offensive capability:
* **Unmatched Seasonal Dominance:** Jordan won 10 NBA scoring titles, a record unmatched by peers or modern players (such as Kevin Durant with 4 or James Harden with 3) [jordan_scoring_0, jordan_scoring_80]. 
* **Extended Multi-Year Peaks:** After winning his first scoring title in his third NBA season, Jordan was not dethroned in any of the subsequent six seasons, and he won his final scoring title in his last season with the Chicago Bulls in 1997–98 [jordan_scoring_80]. His highest-scoring season came in 1990 when he averaged 33.6 points per game [jordan_scoring_80].
* **High-Volume Peak Efficiency:** Jordan combined scoring volume, efficiency, and low turnovers [jordan_defense_0]. He recorded 4 of the only 11 seasons in NBA history where a player scored over 30 points per 75 possessions at +6% relative true shooting (rTS), compared to 1 such season for LeBron [jordan_defense_2720].

**Argument Supported:** Jordan’s scoring titles support the argument that at his apex, he was the league's most dominant individual scorer, repeatedly leading the league in scoring over sustained multi-year stretches [jordan_scoring_0, jordan_defense_0].

---

### 2. LeBron James’s Career Record: The Case for Longevity and Cumulative Output
LeBron’s all-time scoring record is used to argue for unmatched career durability and high-level longevity:
* **All-Time Career Scoring Leader:** LeBron surpassed Kareem Abdul-Jabbar's longstanding total to become the NBA’s all-time scoring leader [lebron_scoring_240, lebron_longevity_560].
* **Two Decades of Elite Production:** His total points record was built across 20 seasons in the league [lebron_scoring_320, lebron_scoring_560]. 
* **Unwavering Yearly Consistency:** Rather than relying solely on high-volume peak seasons, LeBron consistently scored at least 25 points per game in all 19 seasons following his rookie campaign (2003–04) [lebron_scoring_240].

**Argument Supported:** LeBron’s record supports the argument of sustained excellence, unmatched durability, and prolonged elite-level scoring across two decades [lebron_scoring_320, lebron_scoring_560].

---

### 3. Tradeoffs and Separation of Facts from Subjective Judgments
* **Factual Differences:** 
  * Jordan achieved unmatched peak dominance in terms of league-leading individual scoring seasons (10 scoring titles) [jordan_scoring_0].
  * LeBron achieved unprecedented cumulative production over a 20-year span, holding the all-time scoring record and averaging 25+ points across 19 consecutive seasons [lebron_scoring_240, lebron_scoring_320].
* **Subjective Evaluation:** 
  * Whether one favors Jordan or LeBron in broader "greatest" debates depends on subjective weighting: prioritizing peak dominance and the ability to capture individual scoring titles year after year favors Jordan’s profile [jordan_scoring_0, jordan_defense_0], whereas prioritizing career-long endurance, health, and two decades of cumulative scoring output favors LeBron’s profile [lebron_scoring_240, lebron_scoring_320].
